title: Replication: Does LLM-Enhanced Fuzzing Improve Over Standard Fuzzing on Real CVE Rediscovery?

original_idea.body:
# Replication: Does LLM-Enhanced Fuzzing Improve Over Standard Fuzzing on Real CVE Rediscovery?

**Problem:** LLM-enhanced fuzzing papers (PromeFuzz, ChatAFL) evaluate on new discovery tasks. Whether they help re-discover known CVEs faster than standard fuzzing is not tested.

**Direction:** Select 10 CVEs with known trigger inputs (from public PoC repositories). Run AFL++ and an LLM-guided fuzzer on the same targets. Measure time-to-rediscovery for each CVE. Compute speedup ratio.

**Why it matters:** CVE rediscovery benchmarks provide a controlled comparison. If LLM-enhanced fuzzing doesn't improve rediscovery time, its advantage may be in novel discovery only, with implications for how to deploy these tools.

**Relevant context:** PromeFuzz (ACM CCS 2025), ChatAFL, CI Spark. CVE re-discovery benchmarks used in fuzzing research (FuzzBench). Direct comparison on CVE rediscovery not published.
